mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% annualized over the past 3 months signals inflationary pressures that lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the inflation signal, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL and S&P 500 returns over a 3-year rolling window is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in the past month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the labor market signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE and S&P 500 returns over a 1-year rolling window is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a recessionary environment, leading to reduced corporate earnings and investor confidence, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the GDP signal, or if GDP growth and S&P 500 returns show a positive correlation over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the past month signals a strong supply-side response, boosting corporate earnings and investor confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the industrial production signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO and S&P 500 returns over a 1-year rolling window is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an accommodative monetary policy, reducing borrowing costs and boosting corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a FEDFUNDS decrease, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS and S&P 500 returns over a 2-year rolling window is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a strong consumer demand environment, boosting corporate earnings and investor confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the demand signal, or if the joint correlation between HOUST, RSAFS, and S&P 500 returns over a 2-year rolling window is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) coupled with an increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a tightening labor market, leading to wage inflation and increased consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the labor market signal, or if the joint correlation between UNRATE, PAYEMS, and S&P 500 returns over a 1-year rolling window is negative.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, an increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% signals a restrictive monetary policy, increasing borrowing costs and reducing corporate earnings, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the tightening signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS and S&P 500 returns over a 2-year rolling window during tightening cycles is positive.
